AccountOpening.description:
When a mock account opened, at its first read or its last reset, and the cash it opened with. Its account page, the
equity curve and the trades start there. A real broker reports none.
AccountOpening.title: AccountOpening

AiModelResponse.description: My settings' AI model: the models the site offers its users, its default among them, and the one the user's runs use.
AiModelResponse.title: AiModelResponse

ArchiveStatusResponse.description:
The open-data archive's warm-up. A public site reads its daily history from the archive alone, so its runs find no
candidate until `sessions` reaches `needed`.
ArchiveStatusResponse.title: ArchiveStatusResponse

Arithmetic-Input.description:
Two numbers combined: `{"type": "arithmetic", "operator": "multiply", "left": <25-day average volume>,
"right": 1.8}` is 1.8 times that average. Either side may be another arithmetic part.
Arithmetic-Input.title: Arithmetic

Arithmetic-Output.description:
Two numbers combined: `{"type": "arithmetic", "operator": "multiply", "left": <25-day average volume>,
"right": 1.8}` is 1.8 times that average. Either side may be another arithmetic part.
Arithmetic-Output.title: Arithmetic

AttributedProvider.description: An agency whose open data the app reads, by the name it publishes under, and the names of the datasets it reads.
AttributedProvider.title: AttributedProvider

Audience.description:
Whom the deployment serves, and with it which data and brokers it may use. Its properties are the one table of
what each audience allows; the wiring, the trading setup check and the gates of the Web API and the CLI read them,
and nothing else decides by audience.
Audience.title: Audience

AudienceResponse.description:
Whom the site serves and what that allows, as the Audience table says, so the web app offers only what the site can
do. The server still refuses the rest on every request.
AudienceResponse.title: AudienceResponse

AuthStatusResponse.description: What the web app shows first: the first-time setup, or sign-in with or without registration and Google.
AuthStatusResponse.title: AuthStatusResponse

BacktestInputs.description: What a user chooses for one backtest: the period, the cash it starts with and the scores that buy and sell.

buy_score.description: A stock that passes the strategy with at least this score is bought: analysis.min_combined_score_buy in a run.

last.description: The backtest covers every session from `first` to `last`, both included.
last.title: Last

sell_score.description: A held stock at or below this score is sold: analysis.max_combined_score_sell in a run.

BacktestInputs.title: BacktestInputs

BacktestSummary.description: A saved backtest without its days and trades, for the list that compares them.
BacktestSummary.title: BacktestSummary

BacktestTrade.description:
One position of a backtest from its first BUY to its SELL, or to the backtest's last session when it is still held
then. Later BUYs of a held stock add to the same trade. Every field is in every answer, so the Web API's schema
requires each one.

average_cost.description: Per share, the buy fees included, as Position.average_cost.

bought_on.description: The session of the first BUY.
bought_on.title: Bought On

exit_source.description: What sold it: the stop-loss or the score. None while the trade is still open at the last session.

fee.description: The broker fees paid: every BUY's, and the SELL's once sold.
fee.title: Fee

held_sessions.description: Sessions from the first BUY to the SELL, or to the last session.
held_sessions.title: Held Sessions

pnl.description:
Net of every fee and the tax (Position.profit_on_sale). For a trade still open, what selling it at the last
session's close would bring.
pnl.title: Pnl

return_pct.description: The PnL as a fraction of what the shares cost.
return_pct.title: Return Pct

sold_at.description: The SELL's fill price. None while the trade is still open at the last session.

BacktestTrade.title: BacktestTrade

Breadth.description:
How many stocks rose, fell and closed unchanged in one session, and their average change in percent, each stock
weighing the same.
Breadth.title: Breadth

BriefLanguage.description: The language the site's AI briefs are written in. Its value is the web app's locale code.
BriefLanguage.title: BriefLanguage

BriefSentence.description: One sentence of a brief and the held items it rests on. A sentence that cites none is never kept.
BriefSentence.title: BriefSentence

BriefSource.description: One held item a brief was written from, which the brief's sentences cite by its key.
BriefSource.title: BriefSource

BriefSourceKind.description: What kind of held item a brief's sentence cites, so the stock page can name it and link to where it shows it.
BriefSourceKind.title: BriefSourceKind

BriefStatus.description: Where a stock's AI brief of one day stands. One brief exists per stock and Taipei calendar day, for the whole site.
BriefStatus.title: BriefStatus

BrokerFill.description:
One execution as a real broker reports it, in shares: a deal of today, or a past sale with the profit or loss the
broker says it realized, its own fees and tax included.
BrokerFill.title: BrokerFill

BrokerResponse.description:
A broker the signed-in user may choose for a run now, as a run's confirmation names it: the mock account always,
SinoPac for an administrator while the site's login is up.
BrokerResponse.title: BrokerResponse

BrokerageAccountResponse.description: The SinoPac account page: which server the site's login is on, whether it is up, and the account while it is.
BrokerageAccountResponse.title: BrokerageAccountResponse

BrokerageStatementResponse.description: A real broker's account as the broker reports it (BrokerageStatement): every figure is the broker's own.
BrokerageStatementResponse.title: BrokerageStatementResponse

CompanyProfile.description:
What the site holds about one listed company itself, one per stock, each part as its source served it and None
until that source was read. The exchange's company basic data in its OpenAPI gives the names, the dates, the
capital, the people, the address and the website, on every site. MOPS's company basic information gives the main
business and the English name, and the annual report on the exchange's document site is named by its fiscal year
and file: a personal site alone reads those two.
CompanyProfile.title: CompanyProfile

Comparison-Input.description:
Two numbers compared. `crosses_above` and `crosses_below` read both sides at the latest daily bar and at the bar
before it, so `left` crossing above `right` holds only on the bar where it happened.
Comparison-Input.title: Comparison

Comparison-Output.description:
Two numbers compared. `crosses_above` and `crosses_below` read both sides at the latest daily bar and at the bar
before it, so `left` crossing above `right` holds only on the bar where it happened.
Comparison-Output.title: Comparison

ConditionGroup-Input.description: `all` holds when every condition holds, `any` when at least one does. A group may hold other groups.
ConditionGroup-Input.title: ConditionGroup

ConditionGroup-Output.description: `all` holds when every condition holds, `any` when at least one does. A group may hold other groups.
ConditionGroup-Output.title: ConditionGroup

Confirmed.description: Every write repeats the caller's confirmation in its body, so a stray or replayed request without it changes nothing.
Confirmed.title: Confirmed

EarningsTrend.description: A company's held quarters, oldest first, and how long the latest direction of its EPS has lasted.
EarningsTrend.title: EarningsTrend

EpsResponse.description: An EPS figure (Eps): it never comes without its period, kind, basis, source and fetch time.
EpsResponse.title: EpsResponse

EpsUnavailable.description: Missing EPS. It is never 0, and the report shows "Insufficient data" with the reason.
EpsUnavailable.title: EpsUnavailable

ErrorCode.description:
The stable name of each refusal the Web API answers, in `code` next to `detail`: a client switches on it, never on
the words, which may change. Every 403 has its own, so the page tells a missing password from a wrong one, a
refused file, a user who is not an administrator and an installation on a real broker.
ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

ErrorResponse.description: Every refusal: `detail` in words for a person, `code` for the client to switch on.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

ExecutionProvider.description:
A broker a run may order on, chosen when the run starts. Its properties are the one table of what each broker
needs; the order gates, the wiring and the pages read them, and nothing else decides by broker.
ExecutionProvider.title: ExecutionProvider

ExplanationRequest.description: One AI call explains one stock's valuation; the numbers are the domain's, the AI writes only text.
ExplanationRequest.title: ExplanationRequest

Feature.description:
A part of the product the site shows or hides. Its value names its setting under `features` in
config/appsetting.yaml, which holds its FeatureVisibility. The Web API's routes name the feature they belong to
(shows() in d_presentation/web/session.py), and the web app's navigation and pages name the same members, so the
three never disagree about what a feature covers.
Feature.title: Feature

FeatureVisibility.description: Who the site shows a feature to. The Web API refuses the feature's routes to everyone else.
FeatureVisibility.title: FeatureVisibility

FiscalQuarter.description: A calendar-year fiscal quarter in Gregorian years. The MOPS adapter converts ROC years.
FiscalQuarter.title: FiscalQuarter

FollowItem.description: One follow of a decision: the follow's decision, priced when it was followed, and its order.
FollowItem.title: FollowItem

FollowRefusal.description:
Why a run's decisions, or the monthly ranking, cannot be followed into the user's mock account now. The Web API
answers each as its code.
FollowRefusal.title: FollowRefusal

FollowResponse.description: What a follow of the run may take now, and what it took so far.
FollowResponse.title: FollowResponse

FollowReturn.description: What a mock account made since it first followed the ranking, against the benchmark over the same sessions.

account_return.description:
The account's equity at the close of `until` over its equity at the close before `since`, less 1: its fees and tax
are in it. The equity before is the cash the account opened with when it had filled no order by then.
account_return.title: Account Return

benchmark_return.description: The benchmark's total return over the same sessions. None while the history holds no bar of it there.
benchmark_return.title: Benchmark Return

since.description: The trading day of its first ranking follow that filled an order since the account opened.
since.title: Since

until.description: The last session both returns count to. None until the history holds a session from `since` on.
until.title: Until

FollowReturn.title: FollowReturn

FollowScheduleResponse.description: The user's schedule of the ranking follow (FollowSchedule), its last unfinished follow without the record's own texts.
FollowScheduleResponse.title: FollowScheduleResponse

FormulaEvidence.description: One formula of ranking.formulas with what holding it would have done over the period. Every figure is simulated.
FormulaEvidence.title: FormulaEvidence

FormulaRecord.description: One simulated replay of a formula (RankingBacktest) as the comparison shows it, without its curves and rankings.
FormulaRecord.title: FormulaRecord

HeldPositionResponse.description: A position (Position): what is held, its cost, and the gain or loss at its mark.
HeldPositionResponse.title: HeldPositionResponse

HoldingRequest.description: A holding the user enters by hand: shares of a listed stock at their average cost, with the day bought if known.
HoldingRequest.title: HoldingRequest

HoldingResponse.description: One holding of the My holdings page (AnalysedHolding). It is data to read: nothing here says to buy or sell.
HoldingResponse.title: HoldingResponse

HoldingSource.description: Where a holding of the My holdings page comes from. A holding is counted under its one source.
HoldingSource.title: HoldingSource

HoldingsResponse.description:
The My holdings page (PortfolioAnalysis): the holdings of each source read, each counted once under its source, and
the portfolio they make at the last closes the site holds, or at today's quotes where the quote board holds newer
ones. The score ranks two measured factors and forecasts nothing. The score figures are None where the site does
not show the viewer the ranking.
HoldingsResponse.title: HoldingsResponse

IndicatorOutput.description: One number an indicator gives. Which outputs an indicator has is IndicatorKind.outputs.
IndicatorOutput.title: IndicatorOutput

IndicatorReading.description:
One world indicator on one day, as its source served it, beside the reading the site holds of the day before it:
a source serves the first alone, and the site's store answers both.

change.description:
How far it moved from the reading before: for an indicator in percent, the difference in percentage points
(0.05 is five hundredths of a point more); for any other, the share of the reading before (0.012 is 1.2% more).
None without a reading before, or one of 0.
change.title: Change

IndicatorReading.title: IndicatorReading

IndicatorValue.description:
One output of one of the strategy's indicators, `bars_ago` trading days before the latest daily bar.
`{"type": "indicator", "indicator_id": "ind_b", "output": "signal"}` is the MACD signal line of indicator ind_b.
IndicatorValue.title: IndicatorValue

LatestPrice.description:
The latest price: the run's realtime quote when it has one, else the latest daily close. It has no earlier
sample, so a crossing cannot read it; a crossing of daily closes reads `{"type": "market", "field": "close"}`.
LatestPrice.title: LatestPrice

ListedStockResponse.description: A listed stock (Stock). `today` is its official bar of the listing's latest session; None when it did not trade.
ListedStockResponse.title: ListedStockResponse

ManualBuyRequest.description: A manual BUY of one stock the specific-stock run reported, on the broker the request's `broker` query names.
ManualBuyRequest.title: ManualBuyRequest

MarketField.description: A field of one completed daily bar. Volume is in shares.
MarketField.title: MarketField

MarketIndex.description: A market index with a daily history: the own index of the exchange `market` names, kept under that market.
MarketIndex.title: MarketIndex

MarketValue.description:
A field of one completed daily bar, `bars_ago` trading days before the latest one.
`{"type": "market", "field": "volume", "bars_ago": 1}` is yesterday's volume in shares.
MarketValue.title: MarketValue

MonthlyRevenue.description:
One company's revenue of one month, as the TWSE or TPEX OpenAPI's monthly revenue summary serves it, under the
Gregorian year and the month, with the day the exchange served it. Revenues are in thousands of TWD and changes in
percent; a figure the summary leaves blank is None. The company's name, industry and note are as served.
MonthlyRevenue.title: MonthlyRevenue

MovingAverageIndicator.description: `sma` averages the daily closes, `volume_sma` the daily volumes. Both include the bar they are read at.
MovingAverageIndicator.title: MovingAverageIndicator

high_sessions.description: The sessions whose highest total-return level the level at the decision is compared with.
high_sessions.title: High Sessions

Ohlcv.description:
One bar of trading. A daily bar is stamped at its session's 13:30 close in Asia/Taipei, and its volume is in shares.
Every field is in every answer, so the Web API's schema requires each one.

change.description:
The exchange's official change from the session's reference price: the previous close, adjusted on an ex-rights or
ex-dividend day. The exchanges' daily reports and listings and the broker's snapshots report it; a bar without one,
or whose exchange compared its close to no reference, has None.
change.title: Change

Ohlcv.title: Ohlcv

OpenDataAttribution.description:
The credit the Open Government Data License v1 asks of every use, in the form of its annex: each providing agency
with its datasets, the license's notice, and the license's name and address. A use that does not give it holds no
license from the start (Article 3, paragraph 2), so a page that shows open data shows this too.
OpenDataAttribution.title: OpenDataAttribution

Order.description:
The app's record of one order: the decision it executes, what went to (or was refused before)
the broker, and how it ended. OrderPreparation saves it in the `orders` table before it is sent, and OrderExecution
saves the broker's answer, whichever provider ran it.
Order.title: Order

OrderPricing.description:
What prices an order of this deployment, in which phase of the trading day it may be placed and on which brokers.
Audience.order_pricing picks one; OrderGateRule and the follow's window read it, and nothing else decides by it.
OrderPricing.title: OrderPricing

OrderStatus.description: Order lifecycle. Each status lists the statuses that may follow it in next_statuses.
OrderStatus.title: OrderStatus

PageQuotesResponse.description: The realtime quotes a page shows beside its settled closes, from the board every page and user share.
PageQuotesResponse.title: PageQuotesResponse

Permission.description:
What a role may do beyond using its own data. A signed-in user of any role runs every workflow on their own mock
account, watchlist, records and strategies; no permission is needed for that. Each member's docstring names where
it is checked, always against User.permissions.
Permission.title: Permission

PositionValueResponse.description: A position of an account's value.
PositionValueResponse.title: PositionValueResponse

skip_sessions.description: The latest sessions left out, so the newest move does not count.
skip_sessions.title: Skip Sessions

ProblemsResponse.description: Settings the app would not start with (`settings_refused`): nothing was saved; the problems say where and why.
ProblemsResponse.title: ProblemsResponse

QuarterFinancials.description:
One company's figures of one quarter, as its balance sheet, its income statement and its EPS statistics in the TWSE
or TPEX OpenAPI give them, in thousands of TWD: the income figures run from the year's start to the quarter's end,
the balance figures stand at the quarter's end, and the EPS and the book value per share are in TWD. A figure its
industry format does not report, or a statement the archive does not hold, is None.
QuarterFinancials.title: QuarterFinancials

QuarterResult.description:
One held quarter of a company's results as the stock page reads it. The EPS figures are in TWD; the margins and the
debt ratio are ratios of the statements' figures of the year to the quarter's end, None where the company's industry
format reports no such figure or the archive holds no statement of the quarter.
QuarterResult.title: QuarterResult

QuoteRefresh.description: What a page that shows the quote board's quotes is told about asking again.
QuoteRefresh.title: QuoteRefresh

RankedFactor.description: One factor of a ranked stock: its value, and its place among the universe's stocks that have it, 0 lowest to 1.
RankedFactor.title: RankedFactor

RankedStock.description: One stock of a ranking: each factor of the ranking's formula, in the formula's order, and its score.

score.description: The sum of the factors' ranks.
score.title: Score

RankedStock.title: RankedStock

Ranking.description: The monthly ranking at one decision session's close: the stocks to hold from the next session's open.

holds_cash.description: The formula's market filter is on: it holds no stock until the next decision, though the factors are measured.
holds_cash.title: Holds Cash

revenue_month.description: The first day of the month of revenue it read.
revenue_month.title: Revenue Month

scored.description: The universe's stocks with every factor, each of which has a score.
scored.title: Scored

stocks.description: The `top` best scores, best first; equal scores in stock id order. None while it holds cash.
stocks.title: Stocks

universe.description: The stocks that passed the universe at the close: traded, liquid enough and priced at least min_close.
universe.title: Universe

Ranking.title: Ranking

RankingBacktest.description:
What holding each month's ranking would have done over past sessions, as fractions of what it started with, against
the benchmark held over the same sessions. It placed no order and touched no account. Every *_return and drawdown is
a fraction: 0.1 is 10%.

annual_return.description: The compound annual return over the sessions after the first decision, sessions_per_year a year.
annual_return.title: Annual Return

benchmark_curve.description: The benchmark's total-return level over the same sessions, 1 at the first one. Empty when the history lacks it.
benchmark_curve.title: Benchmark Curve

costs.description: The fees and the tax paid, each as a fraction of the value it was paid from, summed.
costs.title: Costs

equity_curve.description: The portfolio's value at the close of its first decision, 1, and at the close of every session after it.

formula.description: The formula whose rankings it held.

holdings.description: The stocks held from the open of each session after a decision, best first, then those that could not be sold.
holdings.title: Holdings

last.description: The period asked: its decisions are the decision sessions from `first` to `last`, its sessions end at `last`.
last.title: Last

tax_rate.description: market.fee_rate on every BUY and SELL, and market.tax_rate on every SELL, when it ran.
tax_rate.title: Tax Rate

turnover.description: The share of the portfolio bought at a rebalance, on average over them. None when it never rebalanced.
turnover.title: Turnover

yearly_returns.description: Each calendar year's return, from the last close before it, or the start, to its last close.
yearly_returns.title: Yearly Returns

years_ahead.description: The calendar years of yearly_returns it returned more than the benchmark. None when the history lacks the benchmark.
years_ahead.title: Years Ahead

RankingBacktest.title: RankingBacktest

RankingExclusion.description: Why the monthly ranking gives a stock no score at a decision session, the first that applies.
RankingExclusion.title: RankingExclusion

RankingFollowResponse.description: The user's mock account against the ranking's latest decision, and what following the ranking did so far.
RankingFollowResponse.title: RankingFollowResponse

RankingFollowRun.description: One ranking follow of the mock account (its run record) with the formula it used, as the settings defined it then.
RankingFollowRun.title: RankingFollowRun

RankingFormula.description:
One way to make the monthly ranking, as the settings name it: the factors whose ranks it sums, the universe it
ranks, how many of the best scores it holds, and when it holds cash instead. It is data alone: the one ranking rule,
its backtest and a stock's standing all read it, and a run that followed a ranking keeps the formula it used.

cash_under_average_sessions.description:
The market filter: the formula holds cash for the month when the benchmark's total-return level at the decision's
close is under its own average of this many sessions. None holds the ranking whatever the benchmark does.
cash_under_average_sessions.title: Cash Under Average Sessions

factors.description: Each is ranked among the universe's stocks that have it, and a stock's score is the sum of its ranks.
factors.title: Factors

top.description: How many of the best scores it holds, in equal weights.
top.title: Top

traded_value_sessions.description:
The universe: the stocks (no ETF) that traded at the decision, closed at min_close or more, and traded
min_traded_value NT$ a session on average over the last traded_value_sessions sessions.
traded_value_sessions.title: Traded Value Sessions

RankingFormula.title: RankingFormula

RankingHoldings.description: A mock account against the monthly ranking's latest decision. A ranking follow sells `left` and buys `lacking`.

decided_on.description: The decision session of the ranking. None before any ranking was read.
decided_on.title: Decided On

held.description: The ranking's stocks the account holds, best first.
held.title: Held

lacking.description: The ranking's stocks the account does not hold, best first.
lacking.title: Lacking

left.description: The stocks the account holds that the ranking does not, in stock id order.
left.title: Left

RankingHoldings.title: RankingHoldings

RatioStanding.description: One valuation ratio at the latest held session against the stock's own held history.
RatioStanding.title: RatioStanding

Reading.description: One sentence of the reading: what it says, and the months, quarters or sessions it counts where it counts any.
Reading.title: Reading

ReadingKind.description:
One sentence of a stock page's reading of its held figures, which the web app says in the reader's language. A
reading with a count names how many months, quarters or sessions it holds for.
ReadingKind.title: ReadingKind

RevenueMonth.description: One held month of a company's revenue as the stock page reads it. Revenue is in thousands of TWD; changes are ratios.
RevenueMonth.title: RevenueMonth

RevenueTrend.description: A company's held months of revenue, oldest first, and how long the latest direction has lasted.
RevenueTrend.title: RevenueTrend

RunReference.description: Which run a trade came from, as the account page names it.
RunReference.title: RunReference

RunSummary.description: The run record (SystemStats) the trading journal saved.
RunSummary.title: RunSummary

SettingChange.description: One setting the settings form changes: the path of its field, and its new value as JSON.
SettingChange.title: SettingChange

SettingField.description:
One setting as the administrator's settings form shows it: its dotted settings path, such as ai.temperature, or an
AI prompt's, such as ai.system_prompt; the control it gets and the group it shows under; the value the file sets,
as JSON, else its default, else null; and what the control offers, all from the settings classes. A value the file
sets that is none of the options or steps still shows, and stays until the administrator picks another.
SettingField.title: SettingField

SettingGroup.description: What an administrator comes to the settings form to do. Each setting shows under one, in this order.
SettingGroup.title: SettingGroup

SettingKind.description: The control the administrator's settings form gives a setting. All but the last three are chosen, never typed.
SettingKind.title: SettingKind

SettingUnit.description: What a setting's number counts, so the form words a value as 2%, 15 minutes or NT$100,000.
SettingUnit.title: SettingUnit

SettingsFile.description: A settings file in config/ the administrator may edit from the Web. Nothing else on disk can be named.
SettingsFile.title: SettingsFile

SettingsProblem.description:
One reason the app would not start with the settings: what, and where when a settings file names a place. The
line and column are 1-based and point at the key the problem is about, or the YAML parser's mark. Never a value:
pydantic's own text can quote the input, which can be a secret from .env.
SettingsProblem.title: SettingsProblem

Settlement.description: Cash a real broker settles for the account on one day: negative to pay for purchases, positive to receive from sales.
Settlement.title: Settlement

SetupRequest.description: The first administrator, with the one-time code the server printed on its console at start.
SetupRequest.title: SetupRequest

SignalResponse.description: A trading decision (TradeSignal) and its evidence; the AI report leaves out the model's raw answer.
SignalResponse.title: SignalResponse

SignalSource.description: Which decision path produced a signal.
SignalSource.title: SignalSource

StockAnalysis.description: A stock page's financial analysis: the three trends read from held data alone, and their reading in sentences.
StockAnalysis.title: StockAnalysis

StockBrief.description:
The AI's short description of one stock on one Taipei calendar day, shared by every viewer of the site: what the
company is, and how the held facts of a recent window of sessions relate to the stock's move over it. It describes
and never advises. One exists per stock and day; its status says whether the AI is still asked. A company card is
one too (BriefKind): it holds the `company` part alone, under the day it was claimed on, and the newest written one
is the company's card. So is the day's world brief, whose `stock_id` is MarketScope.WORLD: it holds the `movement`
part alone, what moved in the held world indicators and which held world news may bear on Taiwan's market.
StockBrief.title: StockBrief

StockBriefResponse.description:
A stock's AI brief as the site holds it. One is written per stock and Taipei calendar day for every viewer, when a
signed-in viewer asks. Every sentence is the AI's wording of held facts and names the held items it rests on; it
describes and gives no advice.
StockBriefResponse.title: StockBriefResponse

StockCompanyResponse.description:
What the site holds about a stock's company itself: its profile, the held items a company card rests on, and the
card. The card is the AI's wording of those items, each sentence naming the ones it rests on; it describes and
gives no advice. A profile's main business and a card's sentences are a third party's and the AI's text.
StockCompanyResponse.title: StockCompanyResponse

StockFinancialsResponse.description:
A stock's financials as the server's open-data archive holds them. The OpenAPI serves only the latest quarter and
month, so the archive holds those it saved while they were served, and nothing before the archive started.
StockFinancialsResponse.title: StockFinancialsResponse

StockNewsItemResponse.description:
One thing said about a stock (Article), as its page may show it: a news site's article and a board's post by title
and address only, since their text is theirs; an open-data item with its text.
StockNewsItemResponse.title: StockNewsItemResponse

StockNewsResponse.description:
What is said about a stock, newest first, as the site's article store keeps it: its material information and the
TWSE news naming it, and on a site that may read them the news sites' articles and the board's posts.
StockNewsResponse.title: StockNewsResponse

StockRankingResponse.description: A stock's standing in the monthly ranking (RankingStanding), with whether the ranking holds it.
StockRankingResponse.title: StockRankingResponse

StockReportResponse.description: One requested stock after a specific-stock analysis (StockReport), as the CLI's Stock Reports table shows it.
StockReportResponse.title: StockReportResponse

StockValuationResponse.description: One stock's valuation before any user assumption (StockValuation).
StockValuationResponse.title: StockValuationResponse

TechnicalObservation.description: Whether the pattern of a rule that adds to the score showed. `rule` is the rule's name in its strategy.
TechnicalObservation.title: TechnicalObservation

TechnicalReport.description:
Result produced by a TechnicalStrategy.

Hard failures reject the stock.
Soft failures reduce technical quality without rejecting the stock.
Observations say, for each rule that adds to the score, whether its pattern showed.
TechnicalReport.title: TechnicalReport

TechnicalRule-Input.description: A condition and what passing or failing it does to the score. The name is a label: the condition alone decides.
TechnicalRule-Input.title: TechnicalRule

TechnicalRule-Output.description: A condition and what passing or failing it does to the score. The name is a label: the condition alone decides.
TechnicalRule-Output.title: TechnicalRule

TechnicalScoring.description:
Each rule's effect applies once, however many conditions it holds: a failed block_on_fail rule rejects the stock
and costs block_failure_penalty, a failed reduce_score_on_fail rule costs failure_score_reduction, and a passed
increase_score_on_pass rule adds pass_score_increase. Passing a block_on_fail rule adds nothing.
TechnicalScoring.title: TechnicalScoring

TechnicalSettings-Input.description:
One owner's strategies and the active one, which every workflow uses. revision counts the owner's saves, so a save
from an older read is refused instead of overwriting.
TechnicalSettings-Input.title: TechnicalSettings

TechnicalSettings-Output.description:
One owner's strategies and the active one, which every workflow uses. revision counts the owner's saves, so a save
from an older read is refused instead of overwriting.
TechnicalSettings-Output.title: TechnicalSettings

TechnicalStrategy-Input.description:
The user's formulas over named indicators, scored together. strategy_id is a stable key and name a label. An
indicator id such as ind_a never holds a parameter: changing ind_a's period changes every rule that reads ind_a,
and a rule that needs a different period reads another indicator.
TechnicalStrategy-Input.title: TechnicalStrategy

TechnicalStrategy-Output.description:
The user's formulas over named indicators, scored together. strategy_id is a stable key and name a label. An
indicator id such as ind_a never holds a parameter: changing ind_a's period changes every rule that reads ind_a,
and a rule that needs a different period reads another indicator.
TechnicalStrategy-Output.title: TechnicalStrategy

TimeInForce.description: How long an accepted order keeps working (Taiwan exchange terms).
TimeInForce.title: TimeInForce

TradeResponse.description: An order that filled at least one share, and the run whose decision it carried out: the followed run for a follow.
TradeResponse.title: TradeResponse

UnfinishedFollow.description: A scheduled ranking follow that left its decision pending (its run record), without the record's own texts but its failure.
UnfinishedFollow.title: UnfinishedFollow

User.description:
A person who signs in, and the owner of their own mock account, watchlist, records and strategies. It holds no
credential: the user store keeps the password hash and the encrypted username and email, and hands back this model
with both decrypted, so the Web answers with it.

permissions.description: What the user's role allows beyond their own data: the web app shows the administration pages from it.
permissions.title: Permissions

User.title: User

UserChangeRequest.description: An administrator's change of one user. A field left out stays as it is.
UserChangeRequest.title: UserChangeRequest

ValuationReportResponse.description: A stock valued at the user's target P/E (ValuationReport). Scenarios exist exactly when its P/E is computable.
ValuationReportResponse.title: ValuationReportResponse

ValuationStanding.description: A stock's P/E, P/B and dividend yield (percent) at the latest session the archive holds, each against its own held history.
ValuationStanding.title: ValuationStanding

Workflow.description: The user-facing operation a run belongs to. Each run has one run id.
Workflow.title: Workflow

WorldIndicator.description:
A figure of the world's markets the site holds one reading a day of, each from a public agency that serves it
without a key: the Taiwan Futures Exchange's daily reference exchange rates and the United States Treasury's
daily yields.
WorldIndicator.title: WorldIndicator

WorldResponse.description:
What the site holds of the world outside Taiwan's exchanges: the world indicators, the world briefs and the world
news. A brief's sentences are the AI's wording of held items, each naming those it rests on; it describes and gives
no advice. A news item's title and summary are its publisher's.
WorldResponse.title: WorldResponse

APIKeyCookie.description: The session POST /v1/auth/sign-in sets: HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/v1, Secure over https.
APIKeyCookie.name: stock_agent_session

info.description:
Runs the stock-agent workflows and reads what they recorded, on the same runtime as the CLI.

Users. Anyone may register (`POST /v1/auth/register`) while registration is open, and signs in with a username or an
email (`POST /v1/auth/sign-in`), which sets the HttpOnly session cookie `stock_agent_session`. A site with a Google
client also signs in with Google: the browser goes to `GET /v1/auth/google/start`, and Google sends it back to `GET
/v1/auth/google/callback`, which sets the same cookie and sends the browser to the app. Public: sign-in,
registration, the first-time setup, the built-in strategies and market data (`/v1/market`). Signed in: every other
read and write, each on the user's own runs, decisions, orders, watchlist, mock account and saved technical settings.
Administrator: the users (`/v1/admin/users`) and the settings form (`/v1/admin/settings`). 401 means sign in: the
session is missing, expired or ended. 403 means signed in but not allowed, and never ends the session. Every write
sends the header `X-Requested-With: stock-agent`, and every write but sign-in, sign-out, registration and setup
repeats `"confirm": true` in its body.

Orders. Full Cycle, specific-stock analysis, valuation and market data never order. Buzz, Intraday and a manual BUY
of a stock a specific-stock run reported (`POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/manual-buy`) send orders through the same gates and
trading journal as the CLI, on the broker their `broker` query names for the whole run: the user's mock account by
default, or SinoPac (`shioaji`) for an administrator while the site's Shioaji login is up, on its simulation server
in dev and test and on the real account in prod, each BUY within trading.max_order_value and the day's within
trading.max_daily_buy_value (`GET /v1/account/brokers` names them). A follow (`POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/follow`) places a
finished Full Cycle's open decisions in the user's mock account only, priced again: at a fresh realtime quote in
continuous trading, or on a site without realtime quotes at the last session's official close while no session
trades. A ranking follow (`POST /v1/rankings/follow`) brings that mock account to the monthly ranking's latest decision,
priced the same way, on the mock account only. No endpoint cancels or modifies an order.

Open data. A public site (`audience: public`) uses only the TWSE and TPEX OpenAPI data the server archives: daily
history and the index trend come from that archive, it has no realtime quote, so Buzz and Intraday answer 403
`realtime_quotes_unavailable`, and it trades on the mock broker only. A personal site reads its daily history and
index trend from the exchanges' own daily reports; without a Shioaji login it has no realtime quote either, so it
answers Buzz and Intraday the same way. A public site reads no news site and no MOPS: the AI step
reads the archived material information, the TWSE news naming the stock and its archived financials, a stock with none
of them is decided on its technical score alone, and every valuation endpoint answers 403 `mops_unavailable`. `GET
/v1/market/audience` answers the site's audience and what it allows, so the web app offers only that.

Backtests. `POST /v1/backtests` replays the user's active technical strategy over past sessions the site already
holds, with the live trading rules on the technical score alone, and saves the result for the user (`GET
/v1/backtests`, `GET /v1/backtests/{backtest_id}`). `GET /v1/backtests/options` names the period it may cover. A
backtest asks no AI, touches no account, watchlist or run record, and never orders.

Rankings. The settings hold the formulas the ranking can be made by (`ranking.formulas`) and which one is active
(`ranking.active_formula`); a save that switches it applies at once, to the ranking, every stock's score, the backtest
and a follow alike. `GET /v1/rankings/latest` answers the monthly stock ranking by the active formula at the latest
decision session the site's daily history holds, and `GET /v1/rankings/backtest?first=&last=` replays it over a period
against the ranking.benchmark_id held over the same sessions. `GET /v1/rankings/formulas?first=&last=` replays every
formula over the same period and costs, and again at a liquidity floor, as the evidence beside the choice. All read only
the held history and the archived monthly revenue, which `just backfill-history` brings back; they ask no AI, touch no
account and never order. `GET /v1/rankings/follow` answers the user's mock account against that ranking, its return
since it first followed it against the benchmark, and its follows with the formula each used; `POST
/v1/rankings/follow` brings the mock account to the ranking, as a run that orders on the mock account only and keeps
the formula it used. `PUT /v1/rankings/follow/schedule` lets the user schedule that follow: from the time they choose,
on the first session after each new decision, the server starts the same run by itself, once per decision, on the
user's mock account only, and its record says the schedule started it. No other run starts without a request.

The server replays `accounts.max_concurrent_backtests` strategy backtests and ranking backtests at once, and one more
waits its turn. A user's request past `accounts.max_backtests_per_user` replaying or waiting answers 429
`too_many_backtests`.

Workflows run in the background, one at a time per user and a few at a time per server: a start answers 202 with the
run id, and GET /v1/runs/{run_id} reports the run's state and its record; another user's run id answers 404. Run the
server with one worker process.
info.title: TW-Stock-Alpha-Agent

get.description:
The SinoPac account as the broker reports it now, for an administrator the site shows features.sinopac_account:
the bank balance, the settlements due, the positions with the broker's last prices and its own unrealized PnL,
today's deals and the sales of the last holdings.realized_days days with the PnL the broker says each realized.
`simulation` says which server this environment logs in to, `login_up` whether the login is up (`statement` is None
while it is down), and `ordering` whether the site lets the user order there (features.sinopac_ordering, off by
default). It only reads: it sends no order, whatever `ordering` says, and it answers no account number.

The brokers the site lets the user order on (features.*) and the user may choose for Buzz, Intraday or a manual
BUY now, the mock account first, each with what a run's confirmation names: a real broker's server and its BUY
limits. SinoPac is listed only while features.sinopac_ordering shows the user ordering there: it is off by default.

schema.title: Response Get Brokers V1 Account Brokers Get

get.description:
Menu 7 on the `broker` account, the mock account by default: the account now, its equity curve, and the account at
the end of `as_of`. A held stock is priced at today's realtime quote where the board of GET /v1/market/quotes holds
one (`live_stock_ids`), which then ends the equity curve too, else at its last daily close. With `since` the
equity curve holds the days from it on only: a page that holds the curve asks for today alone when a quote moved,
since the whole curve of an old account is large and slow to value. It asks the broker for no quote, never orders
and records no run.

403.description: real_broker_refused: a real broker's account, asked by a user who is not an administrator. broker_unavailable: the real broker has no login up on this site now.

post.description:
Opens the user's mock account again with `initial_cash` and no positions; its equity curve and trades start anew
and every decision is open to follow again. No run, decision or order is deleted. 409 while a run of the user
runs, which could order on the account meanwhile.

409.description: run_in_progress: a run of the user is still running.

get.description:
Every order of a run on the `broker` account (the mock account by default) that filled at least one share, since
the mock account opened or every one at a real broker, newest first, each with the run whose decision it carried
out: a follow's with the run it followed. Ask for limit + 1 to know of a next page.

schema.title: Response Get Trades V1 Account Trades Get

403.description: real_broker_refused: a real broker's account, asked by a user who is not an administrator. broker_unavailable: the real broker has no login up on this site now.

get.description:
The settings form: each setting by its dotted settings path, in the order of the settings classes, with how the form
shows it, the value the file on disk sets (else its default, else null), its options and bounds, and whether it
applies only at a restart. The AI prompts of instructions.yaml are fields at their settings paths, such as
ai.system_prompt.

schema.title: Response Get Settings V1 Admin Settings Get

422.description: A settings file does not parse (settings_refused); the problem says where.

put.description:
Writes every change into its settings file in place, every other line, comment and key as it was, opens the app on
the new files, writes them and runs on them at once, when the app starts with them and the password is the
administrator's own; or refuses with nothing written and the app as it was. A change to the value its field shows
is skipped, and changes that change nothing write nothing. Runs that started earlier finish on the settings they
started with. The answer is the form after the save.

schema.title: Response Save Settings V1 Admin Settings Put

403.description: A save without the password (password_required), or with a wrong one (password_refused); by an administrator without a password, a save without a fresh Google authentication made for it (google_confirmation_required).

409.description: The server reloaded its settings after the request started, or another save wrote a file first (settings_conflict); nothing saved.

schema.title: Response 422 Save Settings V1 Admin Settings Put

422.description: The app would not start with the new settings (settings_refused, with the problems at their settings paths), or a change names no field of the form or cannot be written in place (settings_edit_refused).

429.description: Too many wrong passwords from this address (sign_in_throttled); Retry-After says when.

get.description: Every user, oldest first. No administrator sees another user's data: this is the directory only.

schema.title: Response List Users V1 Admin Users Get

patch.description:
Changes a role, deactivates or reactivates a user, or sets a new password. A deactivation or a new password ends
every session of the user at once; their data stays, and a run of theirs already running finishes.

409.description: No active administrator would remain; nothing saved.

get.description:
Where Google sends the browser back: <accounts.public_origin>/v1/auth/google/callback, the one redirect URI of the
OAuth client. A sign-in sets the session cookie and redirects to the app. A settings confirmation grants the save
it was started for and redirects to the settings form with ?google=confirmed. A refusal redirects to the app with
?google= and the reason; nothing is created and no session starts. Either way the flow cookie is cleared.

The browser's way to Google, as a navigation, never a fetch: it sets the short-lived flow cookie and redirects to
Google's sign-in. With `confirmation`, the id the web app made for one settings save, Google authenticates the
administrator again for that save: the start needs the session of an administrator who may edit the settings, and
only that session's save is confirmed. Where the site offers no sign-in with Google, a confirmation comes without
that session (not_administrator), or past the limit per address, it redirects back to the app with ?google= and
the reason.
The signed-in user with their permissions, which the app reads to show the administration pages. 401 when signed out.
My settings: the AI models the site offers, its default, and the one the user's runs use. 401 when signed out.

put.description:
Chooses the AI model of the user's next runs, or null for the site's default. A run already running keeps its model.
A model the site stopped offering later leaves the choice saved, and the runs use the site's default meanwhile.

422.description: The site does not offer that model; nothing saved.

post.description: A new user with the role user: 403 while registration is closed, 409 for a taken username or email, 429 past the limit.

First use only: the administrator, who takes over the data of the single-user version. It needs the setup code the
server printed on its console at start (403 otherwise), so the first visitor of an exposed server cannot claim it.
409 once a user exists. The app then signs in like any user.
Sets the session cookie. 401 for a wrong name or password, one message for both; 429 past the attempt limits.
Ends this browser's session and clears its cookie. Signing out twice is fine.

get.description:
What the web app shows first: the first-time setup while no user exists, then sign-in, with registration while it is
open; and whom the site shows each feature to, which the app reads with the user's permissions to show or hide a page.
The user's saved backtests, newest first: the site keeps the newest accounts.saved_backtests of each user.

schema.title: Response Get Backtests V1 Backtests Get

post.description:
Replays the user's active technical strategy over the period, day by day with the live trading rules, and answers
the backtest, saved for the user. A stock is decided on its technical score alone, as a run decides a stock the AI
is not asked about; a decision made after one session's close fills at the next open. It asks no AI, touches no
account and never orders. The answer comes when the replay is done: seconds, longer for the first one after a start
or while it waits for the server's other replays (accounts.max_concurrent_backtests).

422.description: invalid_request: a field of the body does not validate, and `detail` lists each one. backtest_period_unavailable: the period reaches outside the days the site's daily history can replay, or holds no session; `detail` says which days a backtest may cover.

429.description: too_many_backtests: accounts.max_backtests_per_user of the user's strategy backtests and ranking backtests replay or wait already.

get.description:
What the user may ask a backtest for: the strategy it would replay, and the inputs of the longest one the site's
daily history allows at the live settings. A backtest reads only sessions the site already holds.
One saved backtest of the user, with its days and trades. Another user's id answers 404.

404.description: The user has no saved backtest of that id.

post.description: Deletes one saved backtest of the user. Another user's id answers 404 and deletes nothing.

404.description: The user has no saved backtest of that id.

get.description:
The user's holdings as one portfolio, from held data alone: the SinoPac account's positions as the broker lists
them now (where the site shows the user features.sinopac_account, the user is an administrator and the login is
up), the mock account's (features.mock_account) and the holdings entered by hand. `sources` narrows them; a source
the site does not show the user is never read. Each holding stays under its source and counts once: the same stock
at the broker and entered by hand is two holdings. Each is valued at its stock's last close the site holds, or at
today's realtime quote where the board of GET /v1/market/quotes holds a newer one (`live_stock_ids`), net of the
SELL fee and tax, and carries its standing in the monthly ranking as /v1/market/stocks/{id}/ranking answers it,
or why the ranking leaves it out, and its latest month of revenue with the ranking's acceleration. The portfolio
says its concentration in the holdings.concentration_positions largest stocks, the share of its value the ranking
holds now, and the value-weighted score over the scored holdings with their share. The score figures are None for a
viewer the site does not show the ranking. It is analysis, not advice: nothing here says to buy or sell.

422.description: ranking_unavailable: the site's daily history holds no decision session yet. invalid_request: a bad source.

post.description:
Keeps a holding the user enters by hand, replacing the user's earlier entry of the same stock: one entry per stock.
It is a note of shares held elsewhere: it orders nothing and touches no account. 422 for a stock the listing does
not hold; 503 while the listing is unavailable.
Takes the user's hand-entered holding of the stock off the list. A holding of an account is never touched.

404.description: The user entered no holding of this stock.

get.description:
How many sessions of TWSE and TPEX closes the server's open-data archive holds, and how many the built-in strategies
need. A public site's runs read their daily history from it, so they find no candidate until it holds enough. Public.

The credit the Open Government Data License v1 requires wherever the site shows the TWSE and TPEX open data or what
it computes from it: each providing agency with the datasets the site reads, the license's notice, and the
license's name and address. Public.

Whom the site serves, personal or public, and what that allows, from the one table of each audience's capabilities.
Realtime quotes also need this runtime's Shioaji login, which a personal site may lack. The web app shows only what
the site can do by it; the server still refuses the rest. Public.

The latest session's advancers, decliners and unchanged stocks in the TWSE and TPEX daily listings, each with the
exchange's own change, and the same per industry with the average change in percent. Public.

503.description: The exchange listing could not be loaded.

get.description:
One market index's completed daily bars, oldest first, from the daily history the stock pages share: the history
cache of the exchanges' own reports on a personal site, else the open-data archive. Public. Like a stock's history, it
fetches no realtime quote.
The latest session's most traded stocks in the TWSE and TPEX daily listings, with that session's bar. Public.

schema.title: Response Get Most Traded V1 Market Most Traded Get

503.description: The exchange listing could not be loaded.

get.description:
The realtime quotes the ranking, the watchlist and a stock's page show beside their settled closes, and the ones
My holdings and the mock account are valued at by their own endpoints. Every page and user read one board, which
asks Shioaji once for all of them at most every market_data.page_quote_refresh_seconds while a session trades, and
after the close until one request was answered; outside that it only answers what it holds of today. `refresh`
says when a page asks again. Of a request that names more stocks than market_data.quote_batch_size, what the board
reads at once, the first ones are read and the rest are answered null. A site without a Shioaji login now answers
so and asks nothing. Private: a visitor never makes the site ask the broker. It reads quotes alone, on nobody's
Pipeline: it holds no account and prices no order.
Listed and OTC stocks whose code or name matches, best first, each with its latest official close. Public.

schema.title: Response Search Stocks V1 Market Stocks Get

503.description: The exchange listing could not be loaded.

get.description:
One stock's completed daily bars, oldest first, from the history cache the workflows share. Public. It fetches
no realtime quote: the latest bar is the last settled session's close.

One stock's financial analysis from the data the server holds, with no fetch and no AI call: each held month's
revenue with its change from a year before and the monthly ranking's acceleration (the mean of the latest
ranking.revenue_short_months months over that of the latest ranking.revenue_long_months), each held quarter's
year-to-date EPS, its own EPS, its change from a year before, its margins and debt ratio, and the latest session's
P/E, P/B and dividend yield against each ratio's median over the sessions held. `readings` says what the figures
say by fixed rules, each a kind and a count the web app turns into a sentence. A figure whose history is too short
is null, and its reading says how much is held instead. Changes, margins and the debt ratio are ratios; revenue is
in thousands of TWD. A stock the server holds nothing of answers empty lists. Public.

The AI brief the site holds of one stock, with no AI call: `today` is the brief of today in Taipei if a viewer
asked for one (`status` writing, written or failed), `previous` the newest written brief of an earlier day, and
`stocks_left` how many more stocks may get a new brief today. A written brief has the part `movement`, and
`company` where it was written before the company card took that part over, each a list of sentences with the
keys of the `sources` it rests on: the held figures and the
announcements, news and posts the page shows, by kind, date, title and address. It names the model that wrote it,
when, in which language, and the window of sessions with the close's change over it. Every text is the AI's or a
third party's: show it as text, never as markup. It describes and gives no advice. Public.

post.description:
Asks for the stock's AI brief of today in Taipei, then answers what GET answers. The site writes one brief per
stock and day for every viewer: the first request claims it and makes one paid AI call on the user's allowance,
waiting for the reply; a request made meanwhile, or after it is written, calls nothing and answers what is held. A
failed brief may be asked again. Before the brief, a personal site reads the company's main business and annual
report when they are due, which can take a minute the first time, and the company's card is written when it has
none or what it rests on changed, a second paid call. GET /stocks/{stock_id}/company answers each of them as it is
held, so a page that asks it meanwhile can say how far the request has come. One request at a time works for a
stock: a second one waits for the first and then answers what is held, with no second fetch and no second call. 429
brief_limit_reached when the stock has none today and stock_page.brief.daily_stocks stocks have one; 429
ai_allowance_spent when the user's or the site's paid AI calls of the day are spent. It reads held data only, records no run and
never orders. Private: a visitor never causes a call.

429.description: brief_limit_reached: today's new briefs are spent. ai_allowance_spent: today's paid AI calls are spent.

503.description: The exchange listing could not be loaded.

get.description:
What the site holds about one listed stock's company, with no fetch and no AI call: its `profile`, the names,
founding and listing dates, paid-in capital, chairman and website of the exchanges' open data and, on a personal
site, its main business as filed with MOPS with the page it is from; the `sources` a company card rests on, each
with its address; and the company card, `today` if one was claimed today in Taipei and `previous` the newest
written one of an earlier day. A card is written when a signed-in viewer asks for the stock's brief, or by the
site for the monthly ranking's stocks, and again only when what it rests on changed. Every text is the AI's or a
third party's: show it as text, never as markup. 404 for a code that is not listed. Public.

503.description: The exchange listing could not be loaded.

get.description:
One stock's financials from the server's open-data archive: each archived quarter's revenue, gross profit,
operating income, net income and EPS of the year to the quarter's end, its total assets, liabilities and equity at
the quarter's end and its book value per share, and each archived month's revenue with its changes. Amounts are in
thousands of TWD, per-share figures in TWD and changes in percent; a figure the company's industry format does not
report is null. Both lists are empty for a stock the archive holds nothing of. Public.

What is said about one listed stock, newest first, from the site's article store, at most
stock_page.article_store.shown: the material information its company announced and the TWSE news naming it, with
their text; and on a site whose audience may read them (`news_articles` of /v1/market/audience) the news sites'
articles and the stock board's posts, by title and address. A request first reads what there is to read now into
the store: the open-data archive's items of the last analysis.material_information_days, and the sites' and the
board's, which are fetched when a page asks and then held for stock_page.news_freshness_minutes, one fetch per
stock at a time; a source that fails keeps what was held of it. So the list also holds what the sources no longer
serve, for stock_page.article_store.retention_days. Every text is a third party's: show it as text, never as
markup. Private: a visitor never makes the site ask a news site or the board.

503.description: The exchange listing could not be loaded.

get.description:
One stock's score: where it stands in the monthly ranking at the latest decision session the site's daily history
holds, from the same ranking /v1/rankings/latest answers, by the active formula (`formula`), with no cut at its
`top`. `score` is its place among the scored stocks as a percentile, 100 for the best combined rank; `stock` holds
the formula's factors in order, each with its rank from 0 to 1; `in_top` says whether the ranking holds it. While
the formula holds cash (`holds_cash`) the score is measured all the same and no stock is in the top. A stock the
ranking leaves out has no score and `exclusion` says why: no held history, an ETF, no trade that session, a close
under the formula's min_close, too little traded value, a month of revenue a factor reads not held, or a price
history shorter than a factor reads. The score ranks measured factors; it is no forecast. One stock's standing,
not the ranking's list: it needs no sign-in, and a viewer sees it only where the site shows them both the stock
pages and the ranking (403 feature_hidden otherwise).

422.description: ranking_unavailable: the site's daily history holds no decision session yet. invalid_request: a bad code.

get.description:
The owner's active strategy applied to the stock exactly as a run applies it, with each indicator's value at every
bar it read. Private: it reads the owner's saved strategy.

The active formula's ranking replayed over the decision sessions from `first` to `last`: bought at each next open
in equal weights, at the site's fee and tax, against ranking.benchmark_id held over the same sessions by its total
return. It answers the value of both at every session, their total, annual and yearly returns and drawdowns, the
costs, the turnover, and each decision's ranking and the stocks it held; a decision at which the formula held cash
holds none. It saves nothing, asks no AI and never orders.

422.description: ranking_unavailable: the site's daily history holds no decision session yet; `detail` says what it holds. backtest_period_unavailable: the period holds no decision session the history holds; `detail` says which sessions it holds. invalid_request: a query parameter does not validate.

429.description: too_many_backtests: accounts.max_backtests_per_user of the user's strategy backtests and ranking backtests replay or wait already.

get.description:
The ranking in the user's mock account: which of the latest decision's stocks it holds and lacks, which of its
holdings left the ranking (every holding while the active formula holds cash), whether a follow may start now, its

put.description:
My settings: schedules the user's ranking follow, or turns the schedule off with null. With a time, the site follows
each new decision of the ranking into the user's mock account by itself on the first session after it, from that
time in Taipei and while this site places orders, as a run like the button's (`POST /v1/rankings/follow`): the
same sizing, order gates and journal, on the mock account only, recorded as started by the schedule. It follows a
decision until a follow left the account nothing to trade for it under the active formula, and never one the user
finished by hand; a day whose window it missed, or whose follow ordered nothing or only a part, is tried again on
the next session, once a day, until the next decision supersedes it. A user the site hides the ranking or the mock
account from, or a deactivated one, is followed for by nobody. Setting a time needs the mock account shown;
turning the schedule off does not. `GET /v1/rankings/follow/schedule` answers the schedule as it stands.

from `first` to `last` on the same history, fee and tax, in the settings' order, and again at the liquidity floor
ranking.evidence_min_traded_value. Each row answers the annual return against the benchmark's, the deepest
drawdown, the years ahead of the benchmark and the turnover. The replays run one after another inside one of the
server's replay turns, and each is kept while the history stands. A formula that did best over a past period is not
thereby the best over the next. It saves nothing, asks no AI and never orders.

world indicator's newest reading, the one before it and its change. `briefs`: the written world briefs of the
latest world.brief.shown_days days that have one, newest first; the site writes one per Taipei day from
world.brief.write_at on, and each sentence is the AI's wording of held readings and held news items and names
those it rests on, with the listed stocks a cited item names itself. `news`: the newest world.shown kept items of
the world news feeds, each with its publisher, its time, its address and the feed's own summary. `write_at` is
the Taipei time from which the site writes the day's brief, null on a site that writes none. Every title and
summary is a third party's: show it as text, never as markup. Private.
